localization.pu_shipdealer1_m_cp_pitch_brandcomment_o: Origin ships are statement pieces to be sure. You fly one of these beauties and everyone's gonna know what kind of person you are.
localization.pu_shipdealer1_m_cp_pitch_brandcomment_r: Buying an RSI is a no brainer. These are the people who basically invented space travel. There's a reason they've been around for 800 years.
localization.pu_shipdealer1_m_cp_pitch_brandcomment_t: It's been great to see Tumbrils kicking around again. They're every bit as solid as the old ones, but with all the modern upgrades you'd expect.
localization.pu_shipdealer1_m_cp_pitch_busy_withcusto: I'm actually helping someone right now, but I'll be with you in just a few.
Once I'm done helping this customer find their dream ship, I'll be right over.
Tell you what. As soon as I wrap up over here, I'll swing on by and get you taken care of.
localization.pu_shipdealer1_m_cp_pitch_encouragebrows: Definitely take a look around. Got some great stuff in stock right now.
Take a wander and see what we have. There are some real gems today.
We have a whole bunch of new inventory you're gonna wanna check out. Real nice stuff.
It's real lucky that you came in today. Some of the best selection we've had all year.
Help yourself to a look around and see what we have on offer. I think you're gonna be real happy when you see what we got.
localization.pu_shipdealer1_m_cp_pitch_encouragedecis: This is a big decision so you be sure to take your time.
Take all the time you need. Don't want to rush into anything.
No worries if you need a few more moments to mull things over.
localization.pu_shipdealer1_m_cp_pitch_encourageinspe: Feel free to climb right up and take a poke around.
Now don't be shy, you like something, go ahead and power her up. Get a sense of how she'll feel.
Be sure to make yourself at home. See something interesting go ahead and get on in. Just don't try to sneak off with her.
localization.pu_shipdealer1_m_cp_pitch_encouragesimca: If you wanna take any of the fleet out for a spin, help yourself to our simcab.
FYI, the simcab over there is perfect for taking these beauties out for a test run.
Between me and you, looking is fine, but if you want to know for sure, may I suggest taking a spin in our simcab?
localization.pu_shipdealer1_m_cp_pitch_encouragetermi: We have a few more options available than what's on the floor. Our terminal's got all the details.
If you don't see what you're looking for, the terminal's got our entire inventory for perusing.
Beyond what you can see, we have a few more ships available on the terminal.
localization.pu_shipdealer1_m_cp_pitch_encouragetobuy: Gotta say, I think this might be the ship for you.
If you want my honest opinion. You could do a lot worse than this.
Well, if you decide not to buy right now, I'll try to hold off the others until you change your mind.
It's tough, right? Should you buy right now? Should you take the risk and wait? I mean I know what I would do, but I want you to do what'll make you happy.
So is this the one? I think it might be the one.
Gotta say, buying used is really the way to go. Not only do you save on credits, but with the high-tech engineering that goes into these things, they run good as new for decades.
Buying used really is the smart way to go. Better on the environment, better on bank account, and way less stress. And more importantly, it's new to you.
You wanna know the difference between a new and used ship? Leaving the dealership. Bam. Every ship instrantly becomes a used ship.
localization.pu_shipdealer1_m_cp_pitch_excuse_fromcus: Anyway, you look like someone who knows their ships. You don't need me talking your ear off. Do your thing, and I'll check on you in a bit.
You know, you look like you could use a moment or two to mull things over. Let me go help some other folks and I'll check back in a few.
Look at me, talking your ear off. Tell you what, you keep looking, and I'll be back.
localization.pu_shipdealer1_m_cp_pitch_farewell_nopur: Thanks for stopping by. Come back any time.
It was great having you. Be sure to come back soon and we can talk more.
All right, sleep on it, and we'll talk soon.
localization.pu_shipdealer1_m_cp_pitch_farewell_purch: All right, thanks again. Hell of a purchase.
Look out, everyone! New ship owner coming through!
It was great doing business with you!
localization.pu_shipdealer1_m_cp_pitch_playerexitship: What do you think? Real nice, right?
How about that detailing? It's something else.
I'm just gonna say it. You two look good together.
Hard to say what's better, right? That great exterior, or that real sharp interior.
You can really see the quality once you get inside.
localization.pu_shipdealer1_m_cp_pitch_shipcomment_be: I know what you're thinking. How can a ship that looks that gorgeous cost so little? To be honest, I can't believe it myself.
Those lines, the styling. Even sitting still she looks like she's flying. A real beauty.
localization.pu_shipdealer1_m_cp_pitch_shipcomment_fa: If you wanna talk fast, this speedster can hold her own. The throttle pretty much accelerates by itself.
If you're looking for speed, then you're looking in the right place. You should hear this baby purr when she gets going.
localization.pu_shipdealer1_m_cp_pitch_shipcomment_gr: As good as this ship is, it's hard to believe it's this cheap. But hey, if that's what the price says, that's what the price says.
Depending on which way you want to go, this ship is probably one of the best deals on the floor. Great condition. Great price.
localization.pu_shipdealer1_m_cp_pitch_shipcomment_ha: What's great about this one here is that it works just as hard as you do if not harder.
If you want a ship that is going to be there day in, day out, taking what ever you throw at it, then this right here might be the ship you want.
localization.pu_shipdealer1_m_cp_pitch_shipcomment_ig: You got a good eye. That's some quality craftsmanship right there. They don't make 'em like this any more, I can tell you that.

You know, I shouldn't say this, but this right here might be my favorite in the whole place. Not that anything we sell isn't fantastic, but I don't know... there's just something special about her. You feel it, right?

Okay, picture this, you're traveling to see that special someone. What are you riding in, some random old junker? Or are you cruising along in a top of the line genuine certified pre-owned beauty like this one here?
We get a lot of different vehicles coming and going, but every once in a while we get something in like this one here that really catches my eye.
You can talk specs and figures all day, but sometimes when you look at a ship, you just know its right for you. I say trust that gut.
localization.pu_shipdealer1_m_cp_pitch_shipcomment_sa: Personally, what I look for in a ship, is something that can get me where I'm going safe and sound in one piece. That's gonna be this ship right here.
They say you can't put a price on safety. I say bullshit. Not only did we put a price on it, we put a great price on it. Protection per credit, you're not gonna find much better than this.
localization.pu_shipdealer1_m_cp_pitch_shipcomment_st: I don't know about you, but I can always use some more storage room. That's why this ship is perfect. Plenty of SCU and then some.
If storage is important to you, then you should do yourself a favor and spend some time with this ship. I think you'll be happy with what you see.
localization.pu_shipdealer1_m_cp_pitch_shipnamecommen: Not only is the 300 a pleasure to fly, when you're not flying her, she's a real pleasure to look at. I know I wouldn't kick her out of my hangar.
Promise me one thing, if you wind up getting the 600, you're gonna invite me to one of your parties cause everybody knows that the best parties in the verse are 600 parties.

I'll be honest, I wasn't quite sure what to make of the 85x at first. But now that I've spent some time with her, she's really grown on me. It's got all of origin's attention to detail streamlined down to a smaller package.
You know a lot of the younger people who come in here are interested in the 100. And I mean, why not? Origin comfort wrapped up in a sporty, fun chasis. I see the appeal myself.
Look. I'll be blunt. There's a swimming pool. If that doesn't convince you on the 890, I'm not sure what else will.
The Argo MPUV is a great little workhorse. Functional to a fault.

I've talked to some of the ex-Navy who come in here about the Arrow. Well, to tell the truth, it's more like they talk to me about it. Can't say enough good things. Seems the light fighter makes one hell of a scout ship. Not many serving who haven't had their butt saved by one of these guys.

Considering an Aurora, huh? I like that. People are so eager to over complicate things that they forget that basic doesn't mean bad. The Aurora flies and gets you where you're going. Sounds like the perfect ship to me.
There's a reason the Advocacy's been counting on Avengers for so long. Few ships can match its operational flexibility. The thing's an icon.
She's a killer, isn't she? It's like the Vanduul took a Scythe and shaved it down till all that was left was the bite.
The Bucc's a great little fighter. You toss one into any scrap and suddenly its a whole new game. Cutlass coming at you, you can handle it. Cutlass and a Bucc, forget about it.
I could pretty much talk all day about the Carrack, but I'm not gonna do that. I'm gonna let the ship speak for itself.
Caterpillar's got a ton of storage, and Drake was thoughtful enough to give it few ways to protect it. Plus, I always get a weird thrill when a ship looks like its name.

Everyone loves to argue which Connie is the best, but that's like arguing what amount of free money is the best. What I'm trying to say is that they're such a fantastic ship, you really can't go wrong with whichever one you fly.
The Crucible is some pretty incredible engineering. Thing is basically a flying toolbox. They can fix up most problems a pilot can run into. If that's not a great skill to have, don't know what is.

Solid offense, decent defense, not too shabby of a hold, easy to take care of, and an interesting reputation to say the least. A lot of people think the Cutlass is a great investment, and I'm tempted to agree.

The new Tumbril really outdid themselves with the Cyclone. I had an old homesteader in just the other week telling me that she had been riding in one of the originals for decades, and didn't once think about giving it up until she saw the new ones. Not only did she buy the new one, but she told me that she's gonna keep the old one on her porch just to sit in. How about that?
The Dragonfly is less of a ship and more of a lifestyle.
Oh, is there an Eclipse here? Thing's so stealthy I almost didn't notice it. Just kidding with ya. But seriously, thing's as silent of a predator as they come.

The Endeavor is less of a ship and more of a roaming university. It's all a little bit beyond me, if I'm being honest, but I have it on good authority that if you're in the market for a scientific vessel, this is the one you want.

I love that we have an F8 for sale. I remember when these monsters were for the military only. Just look at the thing. Is that a killer or what? Let's see someone try to mess with you when you're flying one of these.
I think over the years, I've sold more Freelancers than just about anything else. I think it's cause MISC made them real jack of all trades. Plus, they really hold on to their resale value.

Just between me and you, I've always wanted to own a Genesis. I flew on one with my dad when I was ten. We were going to visit my grandmother, and I don't think I had ever been on a ship that big or fancy before. Since then, there's always been a part of me that wonders what it would be like to be a commercial transport pilot. But maybe you buy this one, and then you can come back and tell me what it's like.
The Gladi is a fascinting bit of hardware. For being so streamlined, it carries some serious ordnance. Almost like a light heavy.
Gladius is fast, it's maneuverable, and as all the old timers say, it definitely punches above its weight class.

People are always eager to point out that a Glaive is just a Scythe with two blades, but it is so much more than that. You know the Vanduul clans only let the most dangerous and experienced pilots fly a Glaive?

You know what I've always wondered about the Hammerhead? Do you think they came up with the name first and made the ship match, or the other way around? Either way, it's one of the best patrol ships flying today.
The Hawk is what I recommend to any bounty hunter who comes in. It's got the speed you need to run someone down, and guns to spare once you catch up with them.
The Herald is definitely one of the more interesting ships we have on the lot. It's not every data runner that comes with its own broadcast array.
The Hercules performs as advertised. Its got the power needed to haul vehicles wherever, whenever. No easy feat.
You know, Cal Mason of Squadron 42 flies a Hornet. If anyone knows about fighters, it's that guy.
If you're looking for a hauler, you can't go wrong with a Hull. They were built to handle cargo, and damn if they don't do a good job of it.

You know in Sataball when you sail one to a teammate and they just tap it in, no problem? The Hurricane is the ship version of that. One of you is flying, the other is on the turret, and together you are just taking care of business.
If you're actually in the market for something of this size and power, the Idris is a class all its own. She may not be cheap, but would you trust a cheap frigate?
The Khartu stands out for a lot of reasons, but those crazy Xi'an stairs alone make it a must buy.

The Kraken follows Drake's mantra of why do one thing well when you could do fifty. I've heard of them being used as mini carriers for militias. I've heard of them being used as mobile shopping plazas. Heck, I even heard of one guy who turned the whole thing into some sort of crazy night club. Not that I'm recommending that last one.
If I had it my way, I would be out there flying this bad boy myself. I mean look at those thrusters. The M50 is just begging to be flown.
You know what's funny about the Mercury? I get people wanting to buy it who don't even want to do data running. They just like the way it looks. Hats off to the Crusader designers on that one.

You remember the Mustang commercial? Where risk meets reward? Well, Consolidated took all the risk, and we get all the reward of being able to fly them. Bottom line is that they are just a fun ship to fly.

What a beast, right? You think about the war history on these Nova tanks, and it's amazing that you can just walk into a shop these days and buy one yourself. I mean, I used to play with a little toy Nova when I was a kid, and now I get to sell them.

Apparantly, Aopoa had to modify the Nox for Humans. I guess when Xi'an pilot them, they're bodies naturally enhance the aerodynamics. Our weird Human bodies threw everything out of whack, so they had to reconfigure a lot of things to get it just right for us.
Can you believe that the Orion is a ship that actually flies, and not just some kind of mining station? I mean look at the size of the thing.
The P-52 is a great little scrapper to have around to help in a fight. Nimble. Smaller frame which means its harder to hit. And it's easy on the eyes which never hurts.

The Archimedes is the Merlin's more sophisticated sibling. Everything that makes the P-52 so great but a little bit extra sprinkled on top. Definitely would not be out of place if you take it out to the track.

Did you watch when Silas Koerner introduced these back at the '47 CitizenCon? Seemed like a pipe dream that a ship could just roll up and start spitting out outposts. Crazy genius did it though, right?

If you're looking to upgrade a militia, the Polaris is a no-brainer. It's got the torpedos. It's got the small craft bay. Vanduul see one of these patrolling a system, and chances are those gullets are running for the nearest jump point.
Here's the great thing about the Prospector: you go out there and find the right spot to mine, the ship will basically pay for itself.
Hard to believe that our great great great grandparents were going toe to toe with ships just like this. All I can say is I feel damn lucky that T-Vars are on our side now.
This little buggy is great for getting around crowded areas like hangars or for short trips around the city.
Who would have believed that MISC could make a racer this sexy?
A Reclaimer captain once told me that the only ship she hadn't ever salvaged was another Reclaimer. The things are so tough, they just keep flying.
Redeemer's design is a real winner, and if you're lucky enough to snatch this one up, it could be your next great gunship.
The Reliant isn't any old ordinary ship. MISC shoved the thing just chockablock with Xi'an tech. The way it rotates around feels like something out of a sci-fi spec vid.

I'm pretty sure every captain out there shakes a bit in their boots when they see a Tali drawing near. This is a bomber desinged to inspire fear. The thing was pretty much made to chew through cap ships.

Aegis really got it right when they were building the Sabre. It's light, but it still has enough going on that it can hold it's own. My only complaint is that the name is a bit close to a Cutlass. I keep having people come in who are confused about which one is which. Not sure how that's possible, but there you go.
It may not seem like the obvious choice, but let me tell you, you show up to a fight in one of these badass Xi'an warrior rigs and you are making a bold statement right there my friend.

You know my favorite part of flying a Scythe? The whole thing is just a big F you to all the duul out there. You tried to kill us, and now we're flying your ship and doing it better than you can. It's a real rush.
When it comes to fuel, the Starfarer is the industry standard for a lot of people.
I just learned a little while ago that Terrapin is a kind of turtle. How much more sense does that name make now? You know like how the ship has all this heavy armor plating just like a turtle shell?
Did you know that most new planets found are first explored with the help of an Ursa? They're such a tough and durable rover that it's a natural pick.
This thing is less of a ship and more of a mobile fortress. With its heavy armor, you can deliver a full squad of pain and hurt to just about anywhere that needs an ass whoopin.
The Vanguard Deep Space Fighter. If you got a fight in deep space, this is the ship you're gonna want to be flying.

My nephew just bought himself a Vulcan. Started his own repair service out in Ferron. Refuels, repairs, rearms. He's really doing well for himself. I mean, I was hoping that he would work here with me, but if he's happy that's all that matters, right.
This is the ship you want if you're looking to get into the salvaging game. Plus, you got to admit, the Vulture is just a great name for a ship.
Everybody was excited when Origin first announced they were getting into the open canopy market, and when they finally showed the X1, everybody was even more excited. The thing's got style to spare.
localization.pu_shipdealer1_m_cp_pitch_shiptypecommen: Fighter pilots always think they're the heroes, but when it comes right down to it, wouldn't you rather have a ship that can deliver real stopping power like this bomber can?
If you do any mercenary work or you're just worried about security, than a fighter like this is a great way to put your mind at ease. Good offense is the best defense, right?
Just the other week I was watching Kaizen on the spec, and they were going on about how data is gonna be the future. Seems like this would be the perfect time to get data ship of your own.

I always hear people talking about space superiority, but for my credits, you're gonna want some boots on the ground. That's where a drop ship like this really shines. You can strategically insert a team where you need, when you need.
You hear about that explorer who discovered those ancient ruins a few weeks back in Elysium? I'm pretty sure they were flying a ship just like this one.

I always say, you want to see a genuine smile, fly a fuel ship. You'll never feel as appreciated as you do when you top off someone who moments before had been stuck on the drift. Ships like this are the real lifeblood of the 'verse.
At the end of the day, what you really want to know is, can this ship get the job done? And if you're lucky enough to be her new owner, I think you'll know that answer soon enough.
The way I see it, with as much time as you're gonna spend on board your ship, it really is worth it make sure that you travel in comfort.

It impresses me to no end to think about all the brave men and women out there, risking their lives to help save the lives of others. Takes a real special kind of person to fly a medical ship, no doubt about that.

You know what's great? No matter what the government's doing, who the military's fighting, what system you're in, there's always one constant. People are gonna need resources. That what makes a ship like this such a great investment.
Whether you've been racing for years, or you're just looking to get started, she's got what it takes to take home some trophys. All that's missing is the right pilot.
Now, while all the ships we sell are made to last, there's plenty of them out there that aren't so lucky. Salvage ship like this is always in demand.

Snubs make a great addition to any fleet. You want to hit up a moon on the weekend, or just take a fly around a planet, this'll make a quick work of it, and you don't have to spend all the extra credits on flying out a ship bigger than you need.

Cannot express how happy it makes me every time I get to sell a ship like this. It's a tough life out on the black, and support ships make it a bit better for everyone. You could say flying a ship like this is almost noble in its own way.
localization.pu_shipdealer1_m_cp_pitch_welcome_ig_001: Hey, welcome. Great to have you.
localization.pu_shipdealer1_m_cp_pitch_welcome_newdea: Welcome to New Deal Shipyard. The finest purveyor of pre-owned vessels in all of Lorville.
Hey, welcome to the New Deal.
localization.pu_shipdealer1_m_cp_pitch_welcome_teachs: Hey, welcome to Teach's Ship Shop. Your stop for Levski's best ship deals.
Hey, great to see ya. Welcome to Teach's.
localization.pu_shipdealer1_m_cp_purchase_encourageas: As soon as you're ready to fly, you're new ship will be waiting for you at any of the ASOP terminals.
Once all the paperwork goes through, the ship will be ready and waiting at the ASOP.
All right, I'm having the crew bring it around and your new ship should be all ready for you at the ASOPs whenever you want to take her out.
localization.pu_shipdealer1_m_cp_purchase_paymentresp: Oh, that's tough. Not enough credits, huh? Maybe something else around here is more in your price range.
Funds a little tight, huh? Know how that goes.
I think you just made one hell of a good decision.
How good did that just feel? No rush like buying a new ship.
Let me be the first to congratulate you on your new ship. I hope the two of you will be very happy for years to come.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_bs_chat_convointerupt_i: Oh... yeah... you need a second. Sure.
Where the hell are you going?
Okay, sure. Too much too soon. Need some alone time. Got it.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_bs_general_passing_ig_0: Sorry, could I just slip past?
Just gonna slide on by you real quick.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_bs_general_strangebehav: Hi, sorry, what are you doing?
I'm trying to run a business here.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_cp_chat_smalltalk_ig_00: How you doin'? You good? Good. That's good. I'm good too. Had a bit of a late one last night.

You do any of those Schrader seminars? They really realign your thinking, how you view the universe, and all that. The key to it is a meditation called "goal fixation." Made a helluva a lot of sense. You should look into it.

You know, I'm an aspiring entrepreneur by trade. All this is great and all, but it's just the day job, you know? I do some promotion, artist management on the side. Yeah, I got a bunch of irons in the fire if you catch me. It's just a matter of time before something pops.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_cp_pitch_amenitiescomme: This one even comes with some habitation facilities, perfect if you're gonna be on the drift for a while.
Got an extra seat in there for a co-pilot, can help run secondary ship functions or maybe just act as a backup pilot so you can get some rest.
This one's also got a manned turret, which if you ask me, raises the value ten-fold. I'd rather have a dedicated turret gunner than someone playing a video game remotely.
This one comes fully stocked with missiles. Nothing changes the tone of a battle faster than guidance-locked ordnance, am I right?
Looking for a multicrew ship? This one's a beaut. Crewed one myself a couple years ago before I got this gig.
With all the barriers we put between ourselves and our environments, there's something tremendously freeing about piloting without any. Don't you agree?
You'll also find a convenient ramp on this baby for easy access inside.
Also, who doesn't like to keep themselves presentable? Well that is not a concern here, this model comes with a shower.
This one's for a solo pilot. It's a little bit more work as you have a lot more to pay attention to, but I find there's something satisfying about flying solo.
You've probably noticed the VTOL thrusters on this. They'll give you ultra-precise maneuvering when navigating around a landing pad. And require a lot less room to take off.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_cp_pitch_brandcomment_a: If I can be honest, if you'd asked me five years ago, I'd have told you that Aegis Dynamics was dead in the water as a manufacturer, but nowadays they are everywhere. Don't get me wrong, they make good ships. This is a good ship. But yeah, it's just interesting is all.

There aren't many manufacturers that have the rep that Anvil ships have. From what I hear, they run every design through a rigorous internal review process before even starting production to make sure the ship is exactly what they want to make. Pretty impressive when you think about it.
The Xi'an make interesting ships, I'll give them that. You don't really see lines like this in Human construction.
People don't really mention Argo when talking about prominent manufacturers, but I guarantee, if you go to any kind of work site, you'll probably see this ship there.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_cp_pitch_brandcomment_c: For my money, there's no ship manufacturer doing more exciting things than Consolidated Outlands. Silas Koerner's a true visionary. Ships like this are just proof of that.
One of the things I like about Crusader ships is that they aren't flashy. They aren't trying to redefine the wheel. They're just creating good ships and creating them well.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_cp_pitch_brandcomment_d: You know, people like to give Drake a hard time about the fact that some criminals like to use their ships, but I'll be honest, I've seen outlaws in every kind of ship imaginable. Doesn't change the fact that Drake makes good ships.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_cp_pitch_brandcomment_e: A lot of collectors tend to gravitate to Esperia ships. I'm not into reproductions myself, but just look at it... the level of detail they put into them is pretty staggering.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_cp_pitch_brandcomment_g: I love GreyCat. I'll just say it.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_cp_pitch_brandcomment_k: I actually used to race in a Kruger ship. Long time ago. It was purely amateur, but yeah, I was pretty good. People told me I could'a gone pro.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_cp_pitch_brandcomment_m: I know RSI usually gets the credit for building ships for regular people, but if you ask me, it's MISC. I mean, think about it, look at all the industrial ships they've constructed, how engrained they are with hauling, mining, even racing now. I don't know, MISC seems to be making a run for the title.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_cp_pitch_brandcomment_o: I don't need to say anything, right? I mean, an Origin ship is an Origin ship. Just take a moment, look at that. You know what I mean.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_cp_pitch_brandcomment_r: You can never really go wrong with an RSI ship. It's not the most exciting sales pitch, but it's true. They've pushed innovation for centuries. You don't get to do that if you're making crap.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_cp_pitch_brandcomment_t: Looking for some terrestrial technology? Tumbril's a good brand. Though they just relaunched, the tech's been around forever. I guess why fix what isn't broken.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_cp_pitch_busy_withcusto: Let me just wrap up with my friend here and I'll come on by and check on you.
We got some business to discuss. I'll come check on you in a bit.
I've got a customer at the moment, but don't worry, I'll be with you in a bit.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_cp_pitch_encouragebrows: Why don't you have a look around and see if there's anything you like.
Take a gander and see if something strikes your fancy.
Take a walk around, and just breathe it in, you know. It's a big decision.
I'll leave you to it. Always find it's best to sit back, take in the space and let your ship call to you.
Here's what you do. Just walk the place. If I'm making a decision as big as you're making, I like to take everything in before I do anything.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_cp_pitch_encouragedecis: It's a big decision, so think it over.
Take your time. Think on it.
I'll give you a moment. Maybe go for a walk to think it over. That's always been my trick if I want to clear my head and look at the problem fresh.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_cp_pitch_encourageinspe: Feel free to hop in and take a feel. Don't take off though. <laugh> I'm kidding, you can't.
If you see one you like, then go ahead and try it out. We've got the inhibitors on so don't you worry about crashing or blowing up the shop.
All the ships should be open, so climb in and see how it feels. Odds are, you'll be spending a lotta time in there.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_cp_pitch_encouragesimca: We also have a simcab if you wanna take any out for a spin.
There's a simcab too, if you really want that complete experience of flying the ship.
Feel free to check out our simcab if you wanna see what flying the ship's really like. It's just like the real thing. I promise.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_cp_pitch_encouragetermi: Why don't you step on over to our terminal if you're looking for additional info. That can take care of you almost as good as I can. Promise.
Go ahead and hit up the terminal if you need. We usually have some extra inventory on there that's not on the floor.
You need anything else, check out the terminal. That'll have all those numbers and data if that's what you're into. Me, I'm all about how it feels.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_cp_pitch_encouragetobuy: You got a lot to think about, no question, but not for too long, a deal this good won't last.
Just say the word and I'll start the paperwork, but it seems pretty obvious to me that the two of you are destined to be together.
So what do you think? We got a deal or what?
I mean it's a lot of credits, sure, but what do you really have to think about?
It's your money, but if it were me? The choice feels pretty obvious.
There's nothing wrong with buying used, you know. Every single one of mine I've bought secondhand. At least you know it's not gonna blow up the first time you turn it on.
I don't know why you wouldn't buy used. Sure you don't get the bragging rights of saying it's brand new, but you ask me, used ships got more character.
Honestly if it were up to me, I'd charge more for used ships. They've been out there. Tested. You know they can deliver. New ships? They got nice paint jobs.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_cp_pitch_excuse_fromcus: You know what? I'll get outta your hair. Hunt me down if you need anything.
You excuse me for a moment? Thanks.
Take a moment. Think about it. It's a big decision. Come flag me down if you need anything.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_cp_pitch_farewell_nopur: Come back if you change your mind.
You let me know when you're ready to take that next step.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_cp_pitch_playerexitship: You ask me, you won't know the first thing about a ship or anything unless you spend a little time in the pilot seat.
What'd you think? Really get a sense of what's possible, right?
Already starting to feel like home, right?
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_cp_pitch_shipcomment_be: Quite a looker, isn't she? I know there are people out there that just wanna turn heads. If that's you, I think you found your ship.
Everybody always stops to gawk at this one. Can't blame them really. Sleek lines. Impeccable design. It's a work of art really.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_cp_pitch_shipcomment_fa: I'll level with you. If you're looking to go slow, you need to walk away from this one right here. It's almost a psychological condition. You start up this monster, you'll be peeling metal.
You got an eye for speed, I see. Well, if that's the case, look no further. This one right here can knock paint off a space station. I had a customer even bring one back because it was too intense.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_cp_pitch_shipcomment_gr: I don't know if you've looked at the price tag, but if not, let me be the first to tell you, that this baby is priced to move. I've had three people today asking about her, so if you're interested I'd move fast.
You aren't gonna find a better deal. Not anywhere in the 'verse.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_cp_pitch_shipcomment_ha: Here's what I like about this model here: fortitude. You can take it out, grind away for hours at a time and this baby'll eat that up and ask for more.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_cp_pitch_shipcomment_ig: I'm sensing a connection here. Do you feel that? Yeah, you do. That's my superpower, sensing connections. Makes sense when you sell as much product as I do.

What you're looking at right there is a classic. You get all these people clamoring for the 'newest, hottest thing' but give me worn and tested any day. Everything's great right out of the box, but if you can last, like really last, then you're onto something.
Here's the thing, I could hit you with stats, figures, hull compression strength or whatever, but honestly, the decision's been made. You knew from the moment you looked at her.
For my money, there's nothing I'd rather be piloting than this bad boy right here. It's everything you need, when you need it. In fact, if you're not gonna buy it, I might get it for myself.
You know, someone considerably wiser than me once said, "you don't pick your ship, your ship picks you." I think this one, this one right here is sweet on you.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_cp_pitch_shipcomment_sa: One word comes to mind whenever I look at this one: trust. I know that thanks to dependable construction and cutting edge design, it will get me and my loved ones wherever we want to go and get us there in one piece.

Here's the great thing about this ship. It's safe. I know, I know, that sounds like a dirty word, but let me tell you, safe may not be sexiest marketing slang, but it's what all of us are ultimately looking for. Getting somewhere safe is priceless.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_cp_pitch_shipcomment_st: Looking for a transport? You could do a lot worse than this one. Plenty of open space for hauling whatever the hell you want. I mean, you got so much room you could probably haul a little bit of everything and still have SCU to spare.

One of the great things about this baby here is space. If you're looking to haul, you can't go wrong with this model. I used this very ship to help move my parents into their new home. One of the easiest moves I've ever made.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_cp_pitch_shipnamecommen: Your entry into the world of Origin ships, but don't let that fool you. The 100s got all the excellence and design of its bigger brothers.
Is there anything sexier than a 300 series? The answer to that is yes, the one thing sexier is your 300 series.

Origin's response to RSI's Constellation line. Their goal with the 600 was to find that perfect balance between elegance and function. All you got to do is step aboard and you'll quickly realize that they nailed it.
85x is your weekend, fly over to that artisan deli and grab a picnic type of luxury ship. Simple, elegant, stunning.
If you're looking for a ship that emits success, look no further. But I don't need to tell you that. Look at it. Success is basically forged into the hull.

The MPUV is short for Multi-Purpose Utility Vehicle. Argo has been pumping these things out like crazy. If you go to any kind of factory, hauling or mining facility, I guarantee you're gonna run into ten of them. Needless to say, they're popular for a reason.

You wanna keep it fast and light. The Arrow's your ship. Anvil built her as a combat alternative to the Gladius. Were they successful? Depends on who you ask, maybe you can tell me where you land on it.

People like to sleep on the Aurora. Sure, you line it up against all the other ships in the 'verse and yeah, maybe it's a little weak, but I'll tell you this. I still fly mine every day. How many ships can you say that about?
You gotta love Avengers. For the longest time, everybody would immediately mistake you for a cop when you flew by. Still do in some parts of the Empire probably.

The Vanduul light fighter, lovingly... is that the right phrase? Anyway, created by the artists over at Esperia. This thing's light, it's nimble and a pitch perfect recreation of the original Vanduul design.

You talk to most dogfighters and they'll swear Aegis or Anvil up and down the show, but here's the thing. This bad boy right here is a born scrapper. You got a handful of guns at your disposal and enough speed to keep you out of someone's crosshairs. The rest is up to skill.

I'm not sure if you're one of those who hear the call of the unknown, who have that gnawing desire to discover, to see what lies beyond. If that's you, than this... this is what you want at your side.

Impressive, isn't she? Asymmetrical hull design. Multiple cargo compartments to maximize your capacity. Even some crew living quarters for long runs. You know this ship design is almost a hundred years old? It just goes to show that ships don't have to be pretty to be innovative.
My brother used to say that he'd only really feel like a success if he could buy a Constellation. That, to him, was the pinnacle of space travel. To be fair, it's a helluva ship.
I'll admit, I was a little surprised to hear that Anvil was doing a repair ship. I guess blowing ships up gives you a pretty solid understanding of how to put them back together.

Everybody's got an opinion on the Cutlass. This was the ship that basically put Drake on the map. Gets a bad rap these days, but I don't know. At the end of the day, the ship's versatile, easy to maintain and affordable. None of that sounds bad to me.
Cyclones have been racing around for hundreds of years. Like I always say, if there's something I gotta do planetside, a Cyclone can help pull it off.
I can't ride one of these things. I go too fast. It's just that addictive.
The Eclipse just reeks of pure warfare. I mean, come on, stealth bomber? How bad ass is that? I don't even want to bomb anything but this ship makes me want to.

I was always bad at science. Barely passed my classes to get Equivalency. But I got a ton of respect for people who like studying stuff. You strike me as a real intellectual so this ship would probably make a lot more sense to you.
Oh yeah, the F8. It's what I like to call 'combat sexy.' It's got all the tools you need to absolutely wreck people, and it looks so bad ass doing it.
Probably the most popular ship in the entire MiSC line, the Freelancer's become one of the standard go-to's for haulers, explorers, hell, there are even some couriers who use them.
We've all been on a Genesis at some point in our lives if we've done any kind of interstellar travel. The thing's basically the standard for commercial starliners.

Anvil's Gladiator. A lotta people tend to right this bad boy off as a single-function ship. Good at dropping ordnance and not much else. But they forget that it's a multi-seater with a turret and some decent guns.

Gladius is a bonafide classic. I guarantee you walk up to any person, old or young, and they can pick this ship out of a lineup immediately. It's fought in wars, defended homesteads, everything. The Gladius is the dogfighter by which all dogfighters are measured.

You watch the Lost Squad? This is the exact type of ship that... oh what's his name... that Vanduul commander. I can never pronounce it. Anyway, this is what he flies. It's the variant of the Scythe that they give to their aces. Anyway, you should check out the show. It's pretty great.

Ah, the Hammerhead. Not sure if you've ever seen one of these throw down, but... let's just say wow. It's one of those cap ships that's designed to handle fighters. Anyway, when this thing's firing all barrels, Navy pilots used to call it the Bloom of Death. Cool, right?
Another popular starter ship, the Hawk here's been increasingly popular with amateur bounty hunters or anyone who needs to chase people down and shoot at them.
Drake's data runner is basically the answer to the question of what happens if you strap a cockpit onto a thruster. Not great on turns, but when you're going that fast, who cares.
Odds are if you need to move vehicles from planet to planet, you're looking at one ship. That's this baby right here.

You gotta love the Hornet, right? Take a moment, look at her. Sure, she's a little boxy, but is there any ship more associated with space combat than the Hornet? I don't think so. Maybe the Gladius...
When you only care about cargo space and nothing else. No frills. No amenities. Just cargo. There is a Hull for you.

Speed and guns. A lethal combination in the right hands. You'll need it too. See the Hurricane here... well, to put it bluntly, isn't the sturdiest of ships. In a nutshell, it's a lot better at dishing out punishment than taking it. Not that I'm trying to dissuade you, just that you should know before buying.

If you're looking into buying a frigate, I might have to close early today. Aegis' Idris has been the go-to for everybody from the UEE Navy to megacorps. Show up in one of these and I guarantee you make an impression.
This one was the first ship Aopoa was allowed to sell in the UEE. A modification of the Xi'an military's light fighter, the Khartu'al is agile and surgical.

Thing's a beast, right? A customer of mine, who's very satisfied with this purchase, referred to it as the Human equivalent of the Merchantman. I'm not sure if that's exactly right, but it was a funny analogy.

Thing's a beast, right? Comes as a mobile strike carrier or a mobile marketplace. A customer of mine, who's very satisfied with this purchase, referred to it as the Human equivalent of the Merchantman. I'm not sure if that's exactly right, but it was a funny analogy.
I hope you aren't allergic to speed. It's damn near impossible to keep a beast like the m50 in anything remotely resembling a reasonably safe speed.

The Crusader Reps hate it when I call the Mercury a blockade runner. They think it's implying that it was built for illegal use, but I think it's a compliment. You want to move some cargo or got a courier job but you gotta do it with speed, agility, and pack a nice punch? Mercury's got your back.
If you're looking for a versatile starter ship, I personally recommend the Mustang. Silas Koerner's a personal hero of mine and what he's done with this ship is really something.

Another banger from Tumbril, the Nova is a modern update of the classic battle tank. This thing can shred targets on the ground or in the air. The main cannon is absolutely deafening. It's pretty cool.
If you're looking to blast around in a truly futuristic open canopy racer, I can't recommend the Nox enough. The thing absolutely blazes.
RSI's dedicated mining platform. The Orion's the one you go to when you need large scale mining solutions.
Cool, right? There's something to be said about short-range ships. There's a purity to the experience that I kinda lose when I get in the bigger ones.

I'll be honest, I love taking this baby out for a little spin during breaks. Not this one here, we got another in the back, but seriously, if you're looking for something short-range, the P72 is where it's at. Hands down.

Impressive, isn't it? I'm not sure if you read Silas Koerner's last book, but he talked a lot about technology throughout Human history. You ask me, I think this ship's gonna change things. It's opening up planetary settlement in really exciting ways.

Part of RSI's larger capital ship skunkworks, the Polaris is a corvette-class combat vessel. They released it as part of the UEE's Militia Mobilization Initiative, but private Merc companies and even Corporate Security outfits have been snatching them up.
There are some who say the Prospector's just a starter ship. That it's for amateurs, but here's the rub. Sure, it's not taking down massive hauls, but it's for people who like to work.

Esperia got some ridiculous access to an original Tevarin model to create this line of replicas. You ask me, this looks like something out of a Spec vid. Back in the war, they'd use these to drop boarders on capital ships. How nuts is that?
This little buggy is just what it is. No frills. Dependable and fun as hell to drive. Buddy of mine used to build race tracks for them.
When MISC announced they were jumping into the racing game, I was like 'what?! no way.' but the second you fire up the engines on this puppy... you put away your doubts.
I'll tell you. If you're looking to chew up some debris, you absolutely cannot go wrong with the Reclaimer. This thing is the patron saint of salvage.
The Redeemer was a bit of an experiment for Aegis, but the gunship has definitely found some supporters in the private contractor arena. You ask me, it's because of those rotating nacelles.
MISC's Reliant. If there's anything that signifies how far our relationship with the Xi'an has come, it's this ship. Hell, the damn thing turns vertical like one of theirs.
Here's the thing, if you need to absolutely bomb something into last week. You need a Retaliator. They been doing it for hundreds of years.
Now this, this is a fun ship. While you've got the Hornet for brawling, the Sabre's a more elegant alternative. Fast and precise lethality. I came up with that.
Aopoa's really upping their game in the UEE markets, the San... San'tak... however you pronounce it is supposed to be a scrapper through and through.

Vanduul Scythe. Probably the most known fighter in their armada. This one here? This was captured from a Vanduul defector in Orion. I'm kidding, it's a repro made by Esperia. Looks pretty convincing, right?
One of the big boys of hauling, you can't really go wrong with the Starfarer.

The Terrapin here, it's got a real interesting history, but you aren't here about history, right? If you want to push out beyond the reach of civilization, search for the new, then this is the ship for you.
If you're looking to do some planetside exploration, look no further. The Ursa may not have the speed as something like the Cyclone, but it's rugged, dependable and capable of going anywhere.
Before I start talking, just take a moment and breathe in this ship. <pause> Anvil's Valkyrie. Designed as a heavy troop transport, it's armed, it's armored, it's a killer.

Yeah, the Vanguard here's one of the newer ones from Aegis. They'd had some older heavy fighters back in the day, but they went back to the drawing board with this one to create something thoroughly modern and undeniably deadly.

Aegis' Vulcan. Small, mobile refuel and rearm ship. It's perfect for do-gooder types and budding entrepreneurs. This is one of those ships that pays for itself. You get one of these out on the drift and I guarantee you'll be pulling in credits in no time.

Looking to crack into the salvage game? I don't blame you. There's some good money in it. My dad dragged scrap for years and never hated a day of work. Drake dropped the Vulture here to provide a small, solo option for salvage pilots.

Origin's addition to the open canopy market. Spared no expense either. Aside from the usual Origin quality, they even brought back Alberto Vara to design the thing, so it's not just fast, but beautiful.
localization.pu_shipdealer2_m_cp_pitch_shiptypecommen: Be careful! I'm just kidding. This bad boy's a devastator though. Capable of delivering ordnance with surgical precision. Now, I don't know what you're looking to blow up with this, but I'll just say that whatever it is, it doesn't stand a chance.
Well, if you're looking to tear it up with somebody, you could do a lot worse than this one here. This one's a surefire, Grade-A certified brawler.
After that Origin hack from a few years ago, everybody's putting more stock in securing their data, so ships like this are becoming more and more in demand.

What you're looking at here is a combat juggernaut. It's got firepower, sure. Armor, check. But it's really designed to punch through defenses and deliver troops. Here's the thing though, dropships like this aren't only good for dropping people off, they make excellent extraction ships too.
I always admired people who wanted to explore the universe. I'm too much of a homebody. Take me away from anytime food delivery and spectrum feeds and I lose my mind.
Looking into a fuel ship, huh? You can't go wrong with this one.
Industrial ships are definitely a bit of a niche market, but without fail, I hear good things about this one here.

You can't really put a price on luxury. I mean, you can obviously, but in a larger sense, the ability to travel in the ultimate comfort in an environment designed in the pursuit of pure excellence can't really be quantified.

We don't have a lot of medical ships and to be honest, I'm not as schooled about them, but I've heard good things about this one. Paramedic from Ferron came through last week and gave me the run down.

My old man was a miner. Sixty years sledging rock on planets, asteroids, you name it, he cracked it. I learned early on, that life wasn't for me, but if it's something that you're looking into pursuing, you can't go wrong with this ship here.
Racer, huh? You've got that look. Well, if you need a new rig, this one can definitely sort you out. Speed, agility, all the things that'll pay out in spades on the track.
Good eye. There's a lotta business out there for salvagers. I'm not sure if you're new to the industry or a veteran, but this model here is pretty well regarded.

I'll admit, I got a soft-spot for snub nose ships. Yeah, they don't have the kind of features that the larger ships do, but to me they're efficient. Fast, lean, stripped down. They get down to the essence of flying.
These are the types of ships that keep the universe together. Support ships like her are the backbone of Humanity. If you ask me, it's a proud tradition for those who take up the call.

localization.pu_tieno_cov_f_pmh_collectallcargohaulin: Looks like that was the last piece of cargo. Now, you just got to tackle delivering it all off and we can call it a day.
Hey, just saw you're all loaded up. Good luck on the run and I'll be in touch when you make the drop.
Covalex calling. Looks like you picked up the last of the goods. Great. Now to roll up your sleeves and get it all delivered. Hopefully it goes smoothly.
localization.pu_tieno_cov_f_pmh_missionabandonhauling: Hey, it's El. Is this right? Says you can't do the run after all? I guess so. That's a little weird. But okay, if you can't do it you can't do it. Not sure why I called now…

Hi, El again. Saw you abandoned the contract. Sad to lose you but I admire you advocating for yourself like that. Self-care and all that. If I felt like I couldn't do a job, I would just stick it out and try my best, you know. Speaking of, I better go.
Quitting the job, huh? Oh well. Too much going on to waste time crying over flaky contractors. I'll see you again when you're ready to work.
Hey, saw that you canceled the contract? A little surprised, but it's your call. Just make sure you drop off whatever you collected as soon as possible so no one thinks you're stealing it.

Hey, sorry you're not able to finish this run. Like really sorry. It's gonna be awful finding someone to finish this now, but that's not your problem. Your problem is returning any of the cargo that you still have back to us. I'll leave you to it.

Huh, I'm confused. I'm still seeing that not all the cargo's been returned but I'll go ahead and let Loss Prevention know to switch all the registration over as lost. I sure hope you don't still have any. Anyway, I better get to it.

Okay, I guess all that other cargo's not getting returned then. I'll go ahead and file the paperwork to note the loss. Really hope no one was counting on those boxes getting delivered any time soon. Oh well.
Cool, cool, cool. Got that drop-off logged in. Thanks for taking care of that and I'll talk to you next time.
Okay, see that you handed everything back in. Always nice when I don't have to report a pilot to the authorities. I'll talk to you on the next contract.
All right. Thanks for returning that. Nice to check something off the to-do list. Oh, sorry. Got an actual contractor comming on the other line. Gotta go.
localization.pu_tieno_cov_f_pmh_missionaccepthauling_: Hey, it's El with Covalex. Appreciate you tackling this delivery. Looking at the route, I don't think you'll run into any trouble but then again, maybe you will, so yeah.

Hi, El Tieno, here. Ready to do some cargo hauling? The details were all in the contract so you should be good to go. And the sooner you get it done, the sooner you can do more deliveries for Covalex. Yay…

Hey, it's El, your friendly Covalex contract rep. Looks like you should be all set to go ahead and pick up the shipment. Not to rush you or anything. Though if you did hurry, that'd be great for me. "Your per-hour tuneover rate is too low, El" Or maybe Covalex's expectations are too high? Anyway, I'm gonna go. Bye.
localization.pu_tieno_cov_f_pmh_missionaccepthaulinge: Hey, it's El. This contract's urgent so I won’t waste your time. Or at least I won't waste any more of your time after this. Which I probably didn't need to say. Okay. Disconnecting now.
Hey, it's El Tieno. Just wanted to make sure you saw that this contract's got a clock on it. Focus up, avoid distractions, and you should have no problem getting it done in time.
localization.pu_tieno_cov_f_pmh_missionaccepthaulingf: Hi, El Tieno with Covalex. I was wondering who was going to be the soul brave enough to take on this contract. Guess it was you. Not every pilot's willing to deal with cargo this temperamental, but I'm sure you'll be fine. All right, good luck out there, but be careful, okay?

Heya, Covalex here. Just contacting you about the contract to make sure it was extremely clear that you need to take special care with this cargo. Clients wanted to reiterate that the stuff actually needs to arrive in one piece, so fly with a little bit of extra caution, all right?
localization.pu_tieno_cov_f_pmh_missionaccepthaulingi: Hi, El here. Thanks for picking up this haul. It's been surprisingly hard to find someone who's willing to do an intersystem run. Me, I'd love to go check out another system, but nope, it's a terminal life for me I guess. Anyway, fly safe out there.

Hiya, El Tieno. Taking on an intersystem delivery, huh? I always admire you long-haul delivery pilots for being willing to go through jump points all the time. They freak me out. Space and time just bending around you like that? No thanks. But I'm sure you'll be fine. Talk to you later.

Hi, El with Covalex. Looks like this contract has you heading off to Nyx. People's Alliance does an okay job patrolling the system, but a lot of it can get pretty wild. I suggest sticking to Alliance space when you can and drop the cargo off as quick as possible. The longer you're flying out there with a full berth, the more likely you'll get noticed. Be safe, okay?

Hey, El calling from Covalex. Just saw you picked up that run to Nyx. I'm sure you'll be fine. All those reports about Vanduul moving in there are probably exaggerated for ratings, right? Anyway, good luck.

Hey, El Tieno again. Let's take a look at your contract and… oof. Pyro, huh? Well, I guess we all got to make credits somehow. Just make sure you stay alive long enough to spend them, right? Just kidding. I'm sure you'll be fine. It's not like Covalex would send you there if it wasn't. Hopefully I'll talk to you later.

Hi there. It's El calling from Covalex. Just wanted to check in and thank you for picking up this contract. Not a lot of people want to head into Pyro these days and I can't blame them. So watch yourself out there, okay? Okay.

Hey there, it's El. Thanks for picking up this run, I'm sure it'll be nice to get back to UEE space, huh? Anyway, you've got the details on the haul so it should be pretty straightforward. Good luck, fly safe, and I'll stay in touch.

Hello, hello. It's El. How are things? I see you're going to do another run for us. Very exciting. Looks like this one's gonna take you back into secure space, so that's fun. Anyway, good luck out there.

Hiya! I'm El Tieno, and on behalf of Covalex Shipping, let me be the first to welcome you. I just know you're going to be a great addition to our pilot roster. Though to be honest, I'm still pretty new here myself, so what do I know. Maybe you'll be a terrible contractor. Guess we'll find out! For this job you'll be picking up a bunch of cargo, flying it to where it needs to go, and then dropping it all off. Almost like you're a delivery pilot. Crazy, right? Not sure why my manager wanted me to talk you through this. Seems pretty obvious, really and... I just remembered I'm being recorded for quality assurance... I'm gonna go.
localization.pu_tieno_cov_f_pmh_missionaccepthaulingp: Hi, it's Covalex.Thanks for picking up this contract. I know that the big long hauls usually get the spotlight, but for my credits it's these planetary jobs that keep the Empire running. So, thanks for doing your part and I'll talk to you later.
Hey, El with Covalex here. I am officially acknowledging that you're being assinged this planetery supply run. Cargo's your responsibility now. Don't let it go to your head.
localization.pu_tieno_cov_f_pmh_missionaccepthaulings: Hi, it's El. Thanks for taking this delivery contract. It's a big one so I'm supposed to remind you that "While quantuming between worlds, Covalex strongly urges its pilots to stay in the cockpit the entire duration their quantum drive is enganged." I can't discuss the specific reason why I have to say that, but oof, talk about a mess. I'm sure you'll be fine though. Later.
Okay! El here. Who's ready to do an interplanetary delivery run!? Hopefully it's you. Especially since this is a big shipment with a lot of cargo. So you should probably get started. Have fun.

Guess someone was in the mood to see a bit more of the system. Make sure you hit the bathroom and grab a snack before you head out on this delivery since you'll be in QT for a while. It's El from Covalex by the way. Okay, talk later.

Hey, it's El Tieno. Good to have you on this contract. A lot of pilots either want to stay close to their planet, or do the inter-system hauls so these longer runs can be tougher to staff. Not really your concern though, right? My job is finding pilots, and yours is being one. So get to it.
localization.pu_tieno_cov_f_pmh_missioncompletehaulin: El here. Thanks for doing that run. Everything looks good, so I'll get you those credits. Uhh…. Yeah, I think we're done. Good stuff.

Hey, sorry, been juggling a ton of things but saw that you got everything delivered. I swear I thought you just launched. It's been a day, I'll just leave it at that. Anyway, job's done so I'll get you paid. Talk next time.

Great. All cargo accounted for. You'd be surprised how many delivery pilots can't seem to manage the delivery part. I could use a dozen more contractors like you. I'll make sure your payment gets sent through. You've earned it.

Oh wow. Are you really there? I mean, I said be quick, but that's insane. I'll bet the client's losing their mind. Anyway, I'll see if I can get you a little something extra on top of your pay. Least I can do.

Heya, it's El. My terminal's gotta be bugged because it says you already dropped off the haul. Is that right? It can't be right. It's right. I don't know what kind of wizardry you pulled but that's amazing. I'll see if they'll throw in a bonus with your pay.

Huh, that's all you're delivering? Okay. Better than nothing I guess. Not as good as all of it would have been, but still I'll flag the rest as a loss and send you your adjusted pay. Thanks for the so-so job. Later.

Hey! Congrats on finishing the contra- Oh, wait... You didn't get it all delivered, huh? Okay, that's fine. It happens. I'll start filing the loss prevention paperwork, and send you the adjusted payment. Have a good one.

Whoa. Done already. Ah, but you didn't get all the cargo delivered. No worries. You'll still get paid for what you managed to get done, and I'll flag the rest up as a loss. Hopefully you'll have better luck on the next contract.
Hey, it's El from Covalex. Just saw that you finally dropped off that haul. A little past the expiration date on this one, but that's okay. I can still get you a portion of the payment.

El here. Got word that you were able to get that haul delivered. Appreciate that you saw it through to the end. Client was a little upset it didn't hit within the delivery window, but it's okay. I can still get you something. Take care.
localization.pu_tieno_cov_f_pmh_missionfailhauling_gp: Hey there, it's El. Hate to do this but I'm gonna have to pull that contract from you and mark the cargo as a loss. Bit of a drag, I know, but hey, onwards and upwards, right? Later.

Uh oh. Looks like this isn't your day. I have to pull this contract from you and mark the cargo as a loss, but don't worry, Covalex would be happy to have you tackle a different contract in the future. Have a good one.

Dang. Guess you weren't able to pull this delivery off. Little surprised, but these things happen. Gonna cancel the contract, report the cargo as a loss, and then scream into a helmet until I feel better. Later.
localization.pu_tieno_cov_f_pmh_missionfailhaulingcar: Well… hate to say it, but since it looks like there's actually no cargo left to deliver, the job's over. Now I just got to figure out how to break the bad news to the client. They're gonna be pissed. Better get it over with. Later.
Wait, is this right? Did all the cargo get destroyed? That's not good. We were supposed to deliver that. Guess the contract is canceled. I sure hope the client took out some good insurance.
Hey, it's El. I gotta pull the contract from you. Can't really do a delivery when the cargo's destroyed. Anyway, better luck next time, yeah?
localization.pu_tieno_cov_f_pmh_missionfailhaulingout: Hey yeah, so bad news. Looks like we ran out of time for that haul, so I'm gonna need to pull the contract and mark the cargo as lost. My supervisor's not going to be thrilled. Hope the rest of your day goes better than mine.

Oh no! You ran out of time. That stinks. I know how tricky time management can be. Guess it's something we both have to work on. I'll let Covalex's Loss Prevention team know that the packages didn’t get delivered. Let's hope the next contract goes better.

Hey, it's El. Hate to be the bearer of bad news, but your contract expired so I'm gonna go ahead and mark the cargo as a loss. Always stinks missing deadlines like this. If only there was more time in the day. Speaking of, I better get to it.
localization.pu_tobin_int_m_pmh_prenyxfirstambushover: I figured they'd be a little grateful for saving their asses from the Vanduul, but I guess that's too much to expect. Go ahead and search the body of the ambush leader. Maybe we can find out what they're doing here.
localization.pu_tobin_int_m_pmh_prenyxfirstarriveatlo: Well... Guess the Vanduul also want to know who's been stealing their tech. We're not going to find anything out with them in the area. For now, focus on neutralizing all Vanduul threats and protecting the survivors.
localization.pu_tobin_int_m_pmh_prenyxfirstasteroidba: All right, it's open. Be careful going in. Don't want someone getting the drop on you because you let your guard slip.
localization.pu_tobin_int_m_pmh_prenyxfirstlockedaste: Hey, did a bit of scouting for you. To gain access here, you're going to need to find a working power bank. Maybe search the nearby debris field for a suitable replacement.
localization.pu_tobin_int_m_pmh_prenyxfirstmissionacc: This is Deacon Tobin with InterSec. I'll be running ops on this mission. I'm sure you read the brief, but I find it helps our operatives to have a quick review before stepping off. The Navy has tasked us with chasing down a group of black marketeers who've been profiting off illegally traded Vanduul items. If you keep up with the news, these are the same folks who supplied ASD's infamous Onyx Facilities. Your assignment is to infiltrate a potential storage site and gather as much intel as possible to shut down the group's activities once and for all. I'll be in touch once you hit the provided coordinates. Tobin out.
localization.pu_tobin_int_m_pmh_prenyxfirstmissioncom: That's it. All the data, decrypted and uploaded to the InterSec servers. This has been a huge help. I've only started to process everything, but I see that this group calls themselves the Shattered Blade. Seems they've been operating since the Battle of Vega. Started out scavenging Vanduul wrecks but graduated to going out and hunting down the bastards. We even got a detailed list of contacts and buyers. I've forwarded a copy off to our analysts who are digging through it all as we speak. Once we have something concrete, I'll be back in touch with next steps. Go rest up and yeah, good work today.
localization.pu_tobin_int_m_pmh_prenyxfirstsyncwithmo: Okay, grabbing the data now... Huh. Not getting much. Most of it's encrypted. From what little I can see, there should be a way to unscramble it nearby. See if you can locate a terminal to help unlock this data.
localization.pu_tobin_int_m_pmh_prenyxfirstunencryptf: There we go. I'm seeing dates, credits, transfer codes. This is good, but we're going to need more. According to this, there should be additional encrypted data packets around the site. Your new objective will be to gather all of the data, along with another decryption key. Guess they made them one-time-use for security, but I imagine any other high-ranking members of the organization should be carrying one. You are authorized to use lethal force to secure the data and the decryption key, so roll out and search the rest of this facility, along with their ship and the neighboring base.
localization.pu_tobin_int_m_pmh_prenyxfirstvanduuldes: Nice work taking out that Vanduul.
Good kill. Duul don't like to go down easy.
localization.pu_tobin_int_m_pmh_prenyxfirstvanduuleli: I think you should play along for now. There's a fair chance that they're either one of the black marketeers we're after or at least know something about their operations. Just be ready in case they try anything.
localization.pu_tobin_int_m_pmh_prenyxitemcollectedal: Good. That's the final piece of data we needed. Time to decrypt them at the terminal and get them uploaded to InterSec servers.
localization.pu_tobin_int_m_pmh_prenyxitemcollectedco: All right. That's another encrypted data packet. Keep going and find the rest.
That's one more data packet. Shoudn't be too many more left for you to find.
Another data packet. We're making progress, but for now, focus on finding the rest of the data.
Okay, got another data packet. Good. Shouldn't be much longer to track them all down.
localization.pu_tobin_int_m_pmh_prenyxitemcollecteden: That's the decryption key we need to unlock the data packets.
Decryption key secured. Now you'll be able to upload the data packets.
localization.pu_tobin_int_m_pmh_prenyxmissionaccept_g: Our ship needs your help. Not sure how long it'll last.
Let's go. You gotta protect that ship.
localization.pu_tobin_int_m_pmh_prenyxmissionacceptre: Bet our ship is happy to see you. Do everything you can to keep it safe.
Great, you made it. Now comes the hard part. Good luck protecting our ship.
No time to waste. Better start helping before it's too late.
Need you to step up. Our ship's in serious trouble.
localization.pu_tobin_int_m_pmh_prenyxmissioncomplete: That was close. Thanks for stepping up for us.
Glad you were available to help. Don't know what we would've done without you.
I'll check that off the list. Good work out there.
localization.pu_tobin_int_m_pmh_prenyxreminddecryptio: Hey, we're going to need to find another decryption key in order to access the remaining data. One of the leaders of this smuggling ring should have them.
localization.pu_tobin_int_m_pmh_prenyxrepeatarriveatl: Good. You made it. Go ahead and neutralize the Vanduul and Shattered Blade, then acquire the data packets and decryption key.
All right. Deal with these Vanduul and Shattered Blade, then find the data packets and decryption key.
Those Vanduul really got it out for these Shattered Blade. Fight your way through and then collect the data for decryption.
localization.pu_tobin_int_m_pmh_prenyxrepeatlockedast: No access, huh. You'll have to scout around and find a replacement power bank again.
You'll need to power it up to gain access. See if you can find a usable power bank nearby.
localization.pu_tobin_int_m_pmh_prenyxrepeatmissionac: Deacon Tobin here again. InterSec appreciates your help, but we're hoping to get the latest intel on who the Shattered Blade are selling to. Head out to their storage site and upload the decrypted data packets you find. And don't be surprised if the Vanduul are still interested in them too.

Glad you signed back up for another mission.The Shattered Blade have been continuing their operations, so the Navy wants to keep their data as current as possible. Head back to the storage site, decrypt the data and upload it again. Just be ready to encounter hostiles, Human and otherwise. Dismissed.
localization.pu_tobin_int_m_pmh_prenyxrepeatmissionco: Got the data transferred safely. I'll hand it over to Tech so they can start their analysis. Should have more missions for you soon, so keep ready. Solid work out there today.
localization.pu_tobin_int_m_pmh_tsgmissionabandon_gp_: I'll need to find someone else to take care of this contract.
Look, InterSec can't use people who don't follow through on contracts. If you're gonna work for us, make sure you can commit.
You're walking away from a volatile situation that still needs to be resolved. Please don't do this in the future.
localization.pu_tobin_int_m_pmh_tsgmissionaccept_gp_0: Deacon from Intersec here. These People's Alliance ships seem to keep kicking the hornet's nest. You know the drill. They'll direct once you're on site. Good luck.
Intersec calling. Seems the People's Alliance found another Shattered Blade station and are in need of help. Scramble to the AO as quick as you can and they'll direct from there.
Tobin at Intersec calling. Got another situation between the People's Alliance and Shattered Blade. Head out there and they'll advise.
localization.pu_tobin_int_m_pmh_tsgmissionacceptintro: This is Deacon Tobin. I'll be your op manager over here at Intersec. An anonymous source has indicated that a People's Alliance security ship has been crippled by a Shattered Blade station and desperately needs help. I've contacted their captain and told them that you're inbound with all due haste. They'll establish contact and walk you through what needs to be done when you arrive.
localization.pu_tobin_int_m_pmh_tsgmissionfail_gp_001: Hate to do it, but I'm calling this operation. There is a zero chance of success now.
localization.pu_tobin_int_m_pmh_tsgmissionfail_gp_002: I'm pulling you out. We've lost any chance of completing this mission.
localization.pu_tobin_int_m_pmh_tsgmissionfail_gp_003: This op isn't going to work. We've lost control of the situation.
localization.pu_uee_navy_repui_description: The largest branch and public face of the UEE military. The Navy is responsible for transportation of military resources, maintaining the borders, waging security operations throughout the UEE, and are currently engaged in a war against the Vanduul.

Turns out, one of our suppliers went missing recently. Definitely going to be hard to find a replacement. Really hope they're okay.
I've been thinking about taking a trip out of system for a bit. You know get out there and live a little. Been thinking that I needed some time to reset, you know?

Just got a bunch a free clothes from my cousin the other day. They used one of those Calliope machines, and afterwards upgraded their wardrobe to go with their new body. They're much happier now, and it worked out for me.

Heard there was a cave-in at one of the mines. Sarah and Tobin went over to see if they could lend a hand. Hate to say it, but I wish people would use a bit of common sense when digging. Seems all anyone cares about these days is earning.
I'm a little off. I was regened for the first time a few weeks ago and I don't know, just haven't felt right since. Been having these weird dreams, you know? Anyway, just happy to be alive I guess.
Life's pretty good right now. Nothing I can't handle at least. Got my work, and that keeps me pretty busy. So there's that.
